biography_sections.title: Elizabeth’s monument and estate association
biography_sections.markdown:
The Larne family monument directly establishes Elizabeth as William Glasgow-3324’s wife and records her death on **17 September 1832, aged 60**, supporting birth about **1772**. The former 1765 birth was an unsupported estimate. Stewart is retained as her existing maiden surname; the monument does not itself supply it or her parents.

A widow Elizabeth Glasgow of Larne, administratrix of Jane Stewart of Curran, is a strong identity candidate for this Elizabeth, but the original 1823 assignment does not name her husband or relationship to Jane. No new parent, sibling or child is attached from that deed.

## Source findings

| Source | Finding | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim, Ulster Journal of Archaeology, second series 6 (1900), p.47](https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up), page image inspected | William Glasgow died 5 October 1816 aged 53; his wife Elizabeth died 17 September 1832 aged 60. Names daughters Jane Shutter, Eliza and Mary. | Published monument transcription: direct wife/daughter wording and age-derived birth estimate. Not a contemporary birth register; does not give Elizabeth’s maiden surname. |
| [Registry of Deeds memorial 548257, p.522](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ7-9935-Y), 8 November 1823, registered 17 May 1826, original image 359 inspected | Elizabeth Glasgow of Larne, widow, administratrix of Jane Stewart late of Curran, County Antrim, deceased, assigned a mortgage to Royal Navy lieutenant Roger Brown Curry. Newtown south-side tenement: 21 ft front by 189 ft depth, lane to Larne Quay east, James Mitchell west. Witnesses William Walsh McNeill, attorney, and James Glasgow, writing clerk, Larne. | New estate association and specific title route. Administratrix is an office, not a kinship statement. Widow identification remains strong but unproved; writing clerk’s identity and relationship unresolved. |

## Priority actions

Read Jane Stewart’s administration and the earlier mortgage recited in 548257. Compare the 1824 Elizabeth renewal with this widow and William’s 1815 will without assuming the same property: the assignment is on the south side of Newtown, while the 1779/1832 James–Anne–Jane tenement is on the north side. Preserve these title chains separately.

position.answer: The Larne monument establishes William’s wife Elizabeth and their daughters. Elizabeth died on 17 September 1832 aged 60; the widow administering Jane Stewart’s estate in 1823 is a strong but unproved match to her.
points: The monument records William’s death on 5 October 1816 aged 53; his live structured death field remains the year 1816.

William’s copy will dated 6 December 1815, PRONI D300/1/5/49, remains unread. Its contents and Jane Stewart’s administration may clarify the family and estate connections; administratrix status alone supplies no kinship.
His father, James Glasgow-1509, is probable (76%) from the retained family chronology; no baptism or will clause naming him has been inspected.
Shipping notices from 1787 to 1797 name a William Glasgow or Captain Glasgow as a master trading from Larne and Belfast. This fits his age and locality but is a compatible identification, not proof.

opening: The Larne monument establishes William’s wife Elizabeth and their daughters. Elizabeth died on 17 September 1832 aged 60; the widow administering Jane Stewart’s estate in 1823 is a strong but unproved match to her. William’s copy will dated 6 December 1815 (PRONI D300/1/5/49) remains unread; its clauses are still needed to test the family and estate connections.
